Empirical Research Plan — “School-Bond Investments, Educational Outcomes, and Local Housing Markets in California, 1997-2006”

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Primary design: Fuzzy Regression Discontinuity Design (RDD) that exploits the super-majority vote‐share threshold required for bond approval.  

Why RDD?  
• The probability that a bond measure passes jumps discretely at the statutory cutoff (2/3 before 2001; 55 % after Prop 39).  
• Districts on either side of the cutoff are plausibly comparable in observed and unobserved determinants of outcomes.  
• The design isolates exogenous variation in school-facility spending, enabling causal inference for districts “at the margin.”

Complementary design: Event-study/DID on the RDD sample to trace dynamic treatment effects (t = −5 … +10 years).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Treatment variable  
  Tᵢ = 1 if school-bond measure i is approved (Yes-vote share ≥ statutory threshold); 0 otherwise.

Running variable  
  mᵢ = Yes-vote share (%) − statutory threshold (%).  
  Cutoff c = 0.

Treatment timing / event date  
  τᵢ = election date of measure i. Outcomes are indexed relative to τ (e.g., testscore_{d,t−τ}).

Control group (counterfactual)  
  Districts whose measures narrowly failed (mᵢ < 0) within an optimal bandwidth h around c.

Because the design is fuzzy (passage probability < 1 below and < 1 above c), we estimate a local Wald/2SLS:

  Outcome = β × PredictedPassage + ε,  
  where PredictedPassage is obtained from first-stage RDD of Passage on mᵢ.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A1. No precise manipulation of vote share at the cutoff  
     – Plausible: 1000’s of dispersed voters, secret ballots. We will run McCrary tests.

A2. Continuity of potential outcomes at the cutoff absent treatment  
     – Plausible: districts just above/below c face similar fundamentals. We will test covariate balance.

A3. First-stage relevance (discontinuity in passage probability)  
     – Institutional rule guarantees a jump; can be verified empirically.

A4. Stable Unit Treatment Value (no spillovers across districts within bandwidth)  
     – Potential concern if neighboring districts coordinate facilities; addressed by dropping spatial clusters in robustness checks.

A5. For event-study: parallel pre-trends for just-pass/just-fail districts  
     – We will visually and formally test for pre-trend equality.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. Threats to Identification & Mitigation
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Manipulation/Sorting of turnout or ballot design near cutoff  
    • McCrary density test  
    • Covariate smoothness checks  
    • Exclude elections with known recounts/irregularities.

T2. Multiple bond elections for the same district (serial correlation / dynamic treatment)  
    • Keep the first election within sample window (baseline).  
    • Alternative: cluster SEs at district level and include indicators for prior bond history.

T3. Concurrent policy or economic shocks correlated with bond passage (e.g., state funding changes)  
    • Include year × county fixed effects.  
    • Placebo outcomes (e.g., fire-department response times) to show no jump at cutoff.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# 0. Libraries
library(tidyverse)
library(fixest)     # fast OLS / IV
library(rdrobust)   # RDD estimation
library(lfe)        # for high-dim FE (optional)

# 1. Load data
bond   <- read_csv("ca_bond_elections_1997_2006.csv")      # election level
scores <- read_csv("district_test_scores.csv")             # dist-year panel
house  <- read_csv("zillow_property_values.csv")           # dist-year panel

# 2. Merge & construct running variable
bond <- bond %>% 
  mutate(threshold = if_else(election_date < as.Date("2001-01-01"), 66.67, 55),
         margin    = yes_share - threshold,
         pass      = as.integer(margin >= 0))

# Keep observations within ±20 p.p. for descriptive stats
bond_rdd <- bond %>% filter(abs(margin) <= 20)

# 3. FIRST-STAGE: effect of margin on passage probability
rd_first <- rdrobust(y = bond_rdd$pass, x = bond_rdd$margin)
summary(rd_first)

# 4. Merge outcomes (example: test scores)
panel <- scores %>% 
  left_join(bond %>% select(district_id, election_date, pass), by = "district_id") %>%
  mutate(rel_year = year - lubridate::year(election_date),
         treated  = pass * (rel_year >= 0))

# 5. 2SLS/RD for average effect (Wald)
#   Local sample ±h*, h* from rdrobust first-stage
h_star <- rd_first$bws[1,1]      # effective bandwidth left/right
panel_local <- panel %>% filter(abs(margin) <= h_star, !is.na(treated))

est_iv <- feols(test_score ~ 1 | treated ~ margin, 
                data = panel_local, cluster = ~district_id)
summary(est_iv)

# 6. EVENT-STUDY within RD window
for_evt <- panel_local %>% filter(rel_year >= -5, rel_year <= 10)
est_evt <- feols(test_score ~ i(rel_year, treated==1, ref = -1) + 
                              district_id + year, 
                 data = for_evt, cluster = ~district_id)
iplot(est_evt)

# 7. ROBUSTNESS CHECK: alternative bandwidth ±10 p.p.
alt <- feols(test_score ~ treated | margin, 
             data = panel %>% filter(abs(margin) <= 10),
             cluster = ~district_id)
etable(est_iv, alt)
```

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results (Priors)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
• Test scores: Positive but modest. Based on prior literature, a one-standard-deviation increase in capital stock might raise math/reading scores by 0.05–0.10 SD within 5 years.  
• Property values: Positive. Home prices likely capitalize part of the quality improvement—roughly 1–3 % within attendance boundaries.  
• Broader economy: Small increases in construction employment during build-out phase; long-run effect on local income negligible or slightly positive.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RDD)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C1. Density continuity at cutoff (McCrary) …………………… 1  
C2. Covariate balance around cutoff ……………………………… 1  
C3. Correct functional form & bandwidth choice ……………… 1  
C4. Robustness to alternative bandwidths/polynomials ……… 1  
C5. No spillovers / SUTVA locally ………………………………… 0   (possible geographic spillovers)

Total: 4 / 5 — design is strong but spillovers merit caution.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
This plan combines a local RDD for identification with an event-study framework to uncover dynamic impacts, addresses key threats, and provides implementable R code for replication and robustness.
